editorial.marketOverview: The opening technology selloff persisted into Friday's morning session even as other sectors showed signs of stabilization. Reuters reported Nasdaq down 0.51%, Nvidia down 3.7%, Dow up 0.70% and S&P roughly flat. This divergence reinforces a concentrated AI and semiconductor risk problem, rather than a uniformly accelerating market-wide liquidation. The quotes are reported intraday observations, not synchronized closing prints.
editorial.whatChanged: The incremental evidence is a partial broad-market recovery alongside persistent Nvidia and Nasdaq underperformance. Michigan's final November consumer sentiment was reported at 51.5, revised up from 51.0 preliminary; this modest improvement is not itself a verified catalyst for a sustained QQQ reversal. The curated Open Watch file remains at 174 entries and has no additional new event since the preceding assessment.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The apparent rotation toward non-technology sectors reduces the certainty of an indiscriminate market decline, but the continued weakness in Nvidia supports the existing bearish QQQ/SOX thesis. A Reuters-reported 98.2% probability of a December rate hike remains a risk to long-duration valuations, though direct CME confirmation was unavailable. The earlier +28 bp 10Y–2Y spread is stale, and it would be misleading to present it as live.
editorial.threeDayPath: For the rest of Friday, the base case remains choppy downside pressure in AI-linked equities with potential sharp oversold bounces. Monday and Tuesday should determine whether semiconductor underperformance continues or gives way to broader stabilization. The outlook stays bearish with very high event risk, but no exact price trajectory or probability is asserted.
editorial.bullCase: A credible bullish reversal requires QQQ to reclaim relative strength, SOX to stop lagging, breadth to broaden and volatility to compress. Modestly better Michigan sentiment may support consumer confidence, but is insufficient without market confirmation. Falling yields would help only if accompanied by sustained demand for risk assets.
editorial.bearCase: Continued Nvidia and chip weakness alongside expensive AI financing, restrictive Fed expectations and renewed volatility could pressure Nasdaq across all three sessions. If broader indices lose their tentative stabilization and breadth deteriorates, downside participation could widen. Regulatory and export headlines remain potential catalysts, not confirmed additional market reactions.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Michigan inflation expectations and any subsequent rate-market repricing; capture synchronized QQQ/Nasdaq and SOX changes, semiconductor breadth, VIX/VXN, 10Y/2Y, Brent/WTI matched contracts and direct FedWatch. Monitor Open Watch for genuinely new catalysts and assess Monday–Tuesday confirmation rather than extrapolating from a single morning quote.
